title: Cost Needle feasibility diary: targeted batching, cache, and quant profiles
creator: Maya Kaplan
description:
Objective: run a focused feasibility study to identify a low-risk, high-impact bundle of configuration changes (request shaping / batching windows, KV cache TTL policies, and model quantization profiles) that reduce unit serving cost for mid-range text-generation workloads by ~20-30% while keeping 95th percentile latency and output quality within acceptable guardrails.

Background: multiple cost initiatives surfaced overlapping tactics (batching, cache, quantization) but lack a small, validated playbook teams can adopt without deep infra changes. This ticket captures experiments, risks, trade-offs, and decisions for the initial field pilot (Cost Needle). We aim to produce: a reproducible experiment grid, a validated recommendation (1-2 profiles) per workload class, rollout checklist, and monitoring / rollback playbook.

Success criteria (quantified): baseline unit cost (tokens-in+tokens-out) measured on the last 30 days; target savings >= 20% on candidate workloads; 95th percentile latency degradation <= 15% relative without changes; automated quality regression check (prompt-set BLEU/ROUGE/LLR where applicable) shows <3% metric drift or manual QA sign-off.

Scope: focus on three workload archetypes: conversational chat (short-turn, latency sensitive), assistive completion (single-shot longer output), and high-throughput embedding+rerank pipelines. Experiments will be run against the hosted Redwood API environment (staging) and mirrored on a limited Dedicated pool for capacity signal parity.

Key constraints and trade-offs noted so far: quantization increases throughput/cost savings but may subtly shift logits leading to hallucination risk on knowledge-sensitive prompts; batching increases utilization but can hurt tail-latency during request spikes — we will instrument per-batch latency histograms and adaptive max-batch-time heuristics; aggressive KV cache TTLs reduce compute but may increase staleness for personalization-heavy flows. We will codify safe defaults plus an opt-in aggressive profile.

Artifacts produced by this ticket: experiment grid CSV, benchmark harness scripts, Confluence pilot runbook, Grafana dashboards, example rollout playbook and a sample Canary config. Links included below.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Kickoff: aligned with Eng (Oliver Chen), SRE (Priya Rao), and Applied ML (Liam O'Connor). Agreed on three workload archetypes and initial experiment matrix.

2025-02-18 - Eng PR created to add batch-time sampling hooks and per-batch token accounting: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2384 (WIP). Diego asked for a lightweight feature flag for staging runs.

2025-02-21 - First runs on staging show 18% token-cost reduction with conservative quant profile (int8) + 25ms batching window for embedding rerank pipeline; however tail P95 latency increased 22% for chat archetype under synthetic burst. SRE suggested adaptive batching gating based on qps.

2025-02-25 - Design feedback from Maya Patel (Design) on how to surface policy choices in Console: prefer default conservative profile but provide a "savings advisor" modal with estimated cost/latency tradeoffs. Scope captured as a follow-up UX ticket.

2025-03-01 - PM review: decided to block rollout until we add quality checks for quantized variants on the golden prompt-set (10k prompts). Action: Applied ML to run similarity + hallucination signal (owner: Liam).

2025-03-04 - SRE reported a minor regression on KV cache TTL interaction with autoscaler in dedicated pool; opened incident and mitigation: temporarily increase cache TTL to 60s for test pools while we patch autoscaler logic (incident doc linked).
decision_log: 2025-02-18 - Experimental approach approved: use A/B paired runs with traffic shadowing for low-latency flows; deterministic load replay for high-throughput flows.
2025-02-25 - Approved conservative rollout target: initially allow savings advisor to recommend aggressive profiles only in Dedicated or opt-in tenant scopes (no auto-rollout on hosted tier).
2025-03-01 - Required pre-rollout quality gate: automated golden prompt-set pass rate >= 97% or manual QA sign-off.
2025-03-04 - Temporary mitigation for autoscaler/KV interaction: increase cache TTL on test pools and add an autoscaler safety limiter (engineering task ENG-53312).

SRE (Priya): finish autoscaler patch and validate against cache TTL interaction, target 2025-03-14; surface rollback checklist in Console.
